BiblicalUsage: To hold back, to restrain oneself — Joseph refraining himself before his brothers, and then unable to refrain himself any longer when he made himself known; Saul forcing himself to offer the sacrifice while he waited for Samuel; and Haman refraining himself, holding his fury until he got home. The word is self-control under pressure, for good and for ill.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe restraint is a power, not a weakness, and Joseph shows both sides of it: he held himself back until the right moment, and then he let love out. Haman shows the other side: restraint that only stores up hate. I hold that what I restrain myself for is what my restraint is worth.
